It is well known to everybody that those days we were -- our heads were shaven and we were allowed to change clothes, those people that had clothes to change, who received them from their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you -- was your head shaved before or after you came to talk to Milos Savic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't say this to the Prosecutor yesterday. So before July of 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, it maybe just a transcript problem but at the moment the record states that the question was: "Was your head shaved before or after you came to talk to Milos Savic?" And the answer is "Yes." So the record doesn't reflect whether it's before or after, so perhaps counsel could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought I just asked whether he had his head shaved before, not after, but in the transcript it says both. So did you have your head shaved before you went to see Milos Savic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also on page 73 of yesterday's transcript, describing your appearance when meeting Milos Savic, you said that it took place in July and you said that prisoners had the opportunity to change into the clothes brought to them by their families.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was in July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, what the witness actually said was -- he was asked: "Were you in the same clothes you were arrested in on the 27th of May?" He said "Yes. Only after the interrogation did we begin to get a change of clothes and other things that our families..." Now the question again, as I read it on the transcript, is saying, is being put to the witness that he said he had the opportunity to change his clothes before the interrogation, and that's not what the witness put on the record yesterday. So I think it's mis -- it's misleading the witness as to what he had said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you can clarify that with the witness or rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want to mislead the witness. I just wanted to have these facts clarified. But I'll ask just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you see Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it could have been February or March. I'm not sure. No, not February. No, no, not February or March. It was in May when the exchange of Croats took place, because among that number of 180, there were about 70 Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What year was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992. I can't pin down the month exactly, but it was after we were transferred from SUP to the TO an exchange took place, before we were allowed and before we got lice. That's when this exchange took place. I'm not sure about the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it was Croats who were exchanged, in your words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing. My question was not recorded in the transcript. This refers to your sighting of Tadic in the TO yard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You described, Mr. Mehinovic, your trip to the court in Bijeljina. Was that the first time that you were going to a court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the first time that I went to a military court, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And before that, had you visited a civilian court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were criminal proceedings instituted against you in the former Yugoslavia for the crime of embezzlement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you were convicted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever, before talking to Milos Savic, in any kind of proceedings, give a statement at a police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In those criminal proceedings for embezzlement, you also gave no statement to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'd like to object to this line of questioning. I have no problem with Defence counsel seeking to elicit whether or not a witness has any prior convictions as quite the permissible. But to go into details about the procedures and what he went through, has absolutely no relevance to do with the indictment or this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think my questions are relevant, because they relate to the procedure and the proceedings, since the witness has already confirmed that he had been a defendant in criminal proceedings, I suppose the procedure that applied to citizens living on the territory covered by those laws matters. That's why I want to compare, together with him, the procedure applied then and the procedure in the military court, his experience of the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Unless there's going to be evidence that the procedures are the same, and even if that evidence was elicited, the witness can only inform the Court as to what transpired when he appeared himself, what he was told, what documents he was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to be allowed to pursue this line of questioning because it refers to the procedure he described in answering the Prosecutor's question. I don't want to ask any questions about the previous matter. I just want to know how the criminal proceedings against him were conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I'd object. These are not the same proceedings. This was a criminal proceedings which was conducted in the former Yugoslavia at some time. We're now talking about a procedure in front of some sort of military court, in a time of conflict, by authorities who the Prosecution case is -- that whole question of what law they were applying, who the authorities were. It was -- you know, this is a Republic of Srpska Bijeljina military court. I mean you cannot -- if the Defence want to put evidence before this Chamber, then they can -- about proceedings and that, they can do that through their defence case, if they wish to say that it was lawful or not. And I don't think that comparing criminal proceedings from the former Yugoslavia that this witness may have experienced several, several years ago and the military proceedings to which he was -- appears to have been put through during his time of detention in this time of conflict, where there are so many legal issues outstanding and applicable law, et cetera, are in dispute before this Court serves any evidential evidence and we would object to this line of questioning being pursued as it's not relevant and is not permitted within the Rules on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Prosecutor has asked a number of questions regarding the procedure and presented documents relating to that procedure before the military court in Bijeljina. I don't see any reason why I'm not allowed to ask questions about the proceedings conducted against him. If that is a topic raised by the Prosecution. These are proceedings conducted against -- before a military court. In previous cases, the Trial Chamber was interested in matters of procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's not a question of saying that you can't cross-examine on the proceedings which the witness faced. I think it's a question of interpretation as to what the relevance may be. But the Trial Chamber will allow you, and follow your questions and see whether or not it's proper cross-examination. So you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what sentence was meted out to you in those proceedings for embezzlement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise to the Trial Chamber, but I don't think I will continue to answer this question and similar questions. I will, however, be willing to answer different questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are going to ask questions dealing with military court and the proceedings in Bijeljina which the Prosecution was dealing with, and not these embezzlement proceedings, which the Prosecution didn't deal with. So I'm surprised at your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to explain, Your Honours. In the document introduced by the Prosecution, and that is the record of the hearing of the accused before the investigating judge, it says that the witness we have here has a prior record. That is a piece of information contained in the document introduced by the Prosecution. If the Trial Chamber doesn't wish me to, I will abandon this line of questioning. I'm not insisting on your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the line of questioning dealing with the embezzlement proceedings should be abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept the Chamber's decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were at Milos Savic's office, you two were alone in there, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And as far as I understood, he was typing right there in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You confirmed yesterday the authenticity of your signature on that statement, on both the first and the second page; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you had signed the statement without reading it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During that investigating procedure, was there any coercion or beating by Inspector Savic against you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no coercion, but I was frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So he never addressed to you a word of threat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that your fear was caused by the very fact that you were before an inspector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and because of all the things I had been through in the previous days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you also confirmed yesterday that the contents of this statement is accurate, as far as your interview with him is concerned, apart from the claim that you carried a rifle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he ask you at all about whether you were armed or not on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day he didn't ask me anything about it. He just asked me where I was and what I did at the relevant time, and I told him all I had to say about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you described this statement to Inspector Savic in detail, on page 74, you said that setting off with Kemal Atic and passing by the retirement home, you saw several young people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, young people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Sladjan Grbic and Ibrahim Doslic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think Milan [sic] Savic was there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Junuz Atic was there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you do know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see Sladjan Grbic in Samac after that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by "in Samac." You mean moving around freely?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Bear with me for a moment, Your Honours. I have a problem with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer was not recorded to my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that on that occasion Junuz Atic was there as well? The question was recorded, but not your answer. I'm asking you again so that we can have your answer on record. Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see Sladjan Grbic later when you were detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see him later, after you were released and exchanged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So from the moment of your detention, you never saw him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the Trial Chamber's leave to present a document to this witness originating from the archives of the military court in Bijeljina. I provided copies to the interpreters and I would like the witness to read slowly a part of this document. For the time being, we are only dealing with the B/C/S version, and I would like to have it identified, marked for identification, as in previous similar cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the document about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the statement of Sladjan Grbic given at the police station of Bosanski Samac in August 1992. I believe it was given to Inspector Savic again, but I can't claim with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, this is a statement made by somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a statement by Sladjan Grbic, given in the course of proceedings against this defendant, relating to the facts that he knows relative to the 17th of April and the proceedings concerned were against this witness here. Also, for your information, I am advised that this person is now deceased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So how is his statement -- the contents of the statement going to be tested?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this statement was evidenced in the proceedings conducted against our witness, and it had probative value at the time when the proceedings were conducted against him. I don't see why it has to be tested now, when we are concerned with the credibility of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. My question was alluding to the information you gave the Trial Chamber, that the maker of this statement is deceased. I hope I heard you correctly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you understood me correctly. That can always be verified, and it is always one of the premises of my defence that we can hear the inspector who took the statement. He can confirm whether such a statement had ever been given or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Unless -- no. The Prosecution position is that we object to the use of this document for many of the reasons that Your Honour has already raised in questioning counsel about it. But again, we're in the situation where they're trying to put a statement from a third party to the witness. The counsel has said it was used in proceedings conducted against this witness. We have no evidence to that whatsoever. In fact, the only evidence before this Chamber is that no documents or no evidence or no information of whatsoever kind was shown to this witness during any proceedings. So these are all assertions by counsel. If counsel, as part of their defence case, wish to make this available to the Bench, then they can do that in the defence case. At the moment, this stands here as a statement of a witness who is not only in court but cannot come to court. We have no information about how it was taken, about any truth as to the contents, about when it was used, how it was used. If it's of assistance to the Bench, maybe the witness could say whether or not he's ever seen this document before. But as I said, our position is that we object to it being used at all. And if the Defence want it as part of their Defence case, then let them introduce it during their case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You want to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if you please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During previous cross-examination of other witnesses, they were presented with statements, various statements, by third parties, and that was allowed. For instance, in the case of Witness M, it was allowed for a statement by a third party to be presented to him, and also it is not disputed that such statements can be shown to the witness regarding certain facts which may be important for determining credibility. I believe the facts in question are relevant, and the witness could tell us the very circumstances and comment on the very circumstances relative to what he has told us about the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe, because the other problem we have is we haven't got the English translation. I'll allow you to ask the witness whether he has seen this statement at any stage, and let's see how he answers. And thereafter we will be able to decide whether or not we can proceed with the contents of the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have never seen this statement before, before right here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may add one explanation to assist the Trial Chamber in establishing the following fact: Under the law on criminal proceedings that was applied at the time, statements given at the SUP are not presented at criminal proceedings to any single person. On the contrary; the person involved is questioned to the circumstances. If that is of any help to you. So this witness could never have seen this statement. That's perfectly natural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think so. The point here is that you can't use this statement because it's made by another witness, and the other witness [sic] is that the witness can't be tested on the contents of this statement. So you can't use it with this witness. If you want to use this statement at all, then you had better call somebody who knows something about this statement, somebody like the recorder of the statement perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean that another witness could confirm that one person has said something without the possibility of asking this witness if he knows anything about the incident? I understood you as saying that certain witnesses can be presented with such statements, while others can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. What I was saying is if you want to use this statement at all, since you are saying that the maker of the statement is dead, I was saying that perhaps you can call the person who recorded it. So you can't use it with this witness. And the other question is: Why is there no translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just explained this before. All the documents introduced by my learned friend from the Prosecution that I provided her with were given to the CLSS on the 29th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Including this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Including this one. That is a document that was part of the criminal file in the military court in Bijeljina against this witness here, and that's how I got this entire file, this entire documentation that I presented to the Prosecution. I was promised to get the translation of all these documents by the end of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Anyway, we'll proceed, since you can't use it anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wish to point out, because my colleagues warned me, I want to add that this statement was an official document, part of a court file in Bijeljina, and I got it as such. So it is a document of a certain body, a certain authority, institution. It is a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you've explained that, but you would have to call evidence to that effect, because you are only counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept this, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. I have a few more questions to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this statement be marked for identification or not at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know of a weapon, an automatic weapon, called Zagi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Kemal Atic have an automatic weapon of any kind on him on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did have some kind of weapon, but I don't remember the type or the make.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he have several weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember. He had a large, loose jacket, which made him look big, and I don't know what he carried.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you some questions about the proceedings before the court in Bijeljina. You said that you had only received a verbal invitation from the competent persons in the prison that you should go to the court in Bijeljina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that under the regulations applicable at the time, no enactment or indictments are receivable by the person who is to appear before an investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just have that struck again. We've had this ongoing debate about what was or was not applicable at the time. That's in dispute before this Chamber. And also, I don't believe counsel has established that this witness who was a baker and owned restaurants and was based in the food service industry would have any insight, knowledge, into the law contained in military procedure. I think the question is inappropriate and it's simply again an attempt to put into evidence by Defence counsel something that is not yet in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. The objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness already gave me the answer, but I would like to remind the Prosecutor that the witness earlier, when asked by the Prosecutor, when he was shown a document, the document P55, that when he said that he thought that that document was not legally binding -- was not fair.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, I will not be asking any more questions about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Lukic, the witness may go on speaking and make his own conclusion. That does not mean that the Trial Chamber has accepted the conclusion of the witness. I remember that when he said it was not clear, I remember that, but that does not mean his conclusions are accepted by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had no doubts, but I would still like him to explain his legal views.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is as follows: You are a baker; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're not a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you know that for that criminal offence the penalty was the death penalty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because in the camp we had competent people who knew about these things. They had -- some of them had completed law school, so they knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when you were with the judges, you were told what you were being prosecuted for or charged with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I read the decision that I got, and I asked people what that was, and I asked to have it explained to me later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of a decision was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The decision that I was guilty. And what happened later, there was no explanation. And I don't know, but I think that the Court still has this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were answering the question of the Prosecutor, you said that you did not receive any decision by the Court. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I might have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that means that in prison you received the decision of the Court, in which you were explained that you were being charged with a certain criminal offence? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you found out that the penalty for that crime was the death penalty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 84 of yesterday's transcript, you said that in this room where the judge was, except for the two people that brought you in, there were two more people. Is that correct? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. In the area of the court, or where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the courtroom, in the room where the judge was, how many people were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With me there were seven people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please remember who was there? I will say what I understood -- or actually, maybe you could just explain it once again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of me there were two persons. On the left and the right-hand side, there was one person -- there was one person each, and then there was also one person on my left and on my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But this was not a trial with a jury?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No evidence was led; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there a note taker present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see any note taker.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to present to the witness once again P55 ter. I would like you to turn to page 2. In the middle there it says, under number 14, if you could please read out what it says there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Convicted."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Above that there's a question. It says there something by 14?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Has he ever been where and why convicted?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the judge ask you at this moment whether you have ever been convicted before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He has not asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you -- have you -- were you asked whether you were a baker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read on the same page, under 10, what it says there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Under 8. Interpreter correction. Under 8.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Occupation, baker.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please look more closer at this document. Could you please tell us whether this is your signature. I think yesterday you said that it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also you said this morning to the Prosecutor that you might have signed something but you were unsure because you were scared.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where you were signing these? In the courtroom or in the hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I'm not certain, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And again, Your Honour, I just wanted to have the counsel correct his question. His question is: "Do you remember signing these?" The witness has not said that he signed these. He said it was his signature. He remembers signing something. Whether or not it is these he remembers signing is the whole -- you know, it's up for debate. It's not -- he doesn't have that clear a memory. So where he remembers signing something is another question, but I think the witness has said he really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. You understood what Ms. Reidy has pointed out?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have the transcript in front of me of today's statements and questions, but that's why I wanted to clear this up. Since he said that he was also standing in the hall, I asked him whether he might have remembered that he signed it there, and he said, well, he doesn't, and therefore I don't think there was anything wrong with my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read on page 3, which is actually marked page 2, but in reality it's actually page 3 -- you read to the Prosecutor this part here that's highlighted. Could you please read what it says two lines above this area that you have read out, just what it says in capital letters and above. That's what I'm interested in, because this is not something that you read out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean this thing here that says Atic Kemal? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You read these parts that were highlighted, but the parts above it, what does it say, and also the part above?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You mean the decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Correct. And then what does it say above that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean above it? Would you like me to read the whole paragraph? Where should I start from? I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the line above the word "decision."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can show it to the witness and show him the line, so that we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then the witness will have to wait until you get your microphone on. So the witness should wait -- yes. The witness can go ahead and read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The investigating judge brings --"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then it says there in capital letters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Decision."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the line above that one, the last sentence, the last sentence in that paragraph, if you could please read that one out, slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did you say above?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says -- it starts with, "After the war events in Bosanski Samac..." That is the very last sentence of the whole big paragraph: "After the war events in Bosanski Samac ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "After the war events in Bosanski Samac, and especially the work obligation, I worked in the village Zaselica and Pisari. I do not know this village."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You still claim that you have not said a single word to the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because Zaselica does not exist in the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in Pisari you were digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That you confirmed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This fact about Pisari and digging trenches, you didn't mention this to Savic in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he didn't ask me about that. He asked me about that particular day: Where I was going and where I was moving on the day of April 17th of 1992. He wasn't interested in the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the investigating judge put something into the record that you did not say to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think it's true that I said this, because he didn't ask me about the days that I was going to work under the work obligation. I don't think that was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But he still guessed that you were working as part of the work obligation in Pisari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course he knew, because he was the one that organised it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you can't put that to the witness, whether or not the investigating judge guessed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: There are a million different ways he could have known that, particularly because he was part of the same authorities that forced this witness to dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The investigating judge -- I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The investigating judge entered into the record the fact that you were working in Pisari, but you didn't mention this fact to Milos Savic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see that now, but I have no idea what he was entering. He did not ask me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were at Milos Savic's and at the investigating judge, you signed more than once a record; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it cannot be -- there is no doubt that it is your signature, the signature that is on the statement of the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I already said once that we were not allowed to read what was said on the document. We were only allowed to sign the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you just to read one part of that statement, on page 2, second paragraph -- actually, last paragraph, on the very bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The defendant has been advised -- the defendant has been informed that he was appointed counsel ex officio, Krunic Ziko, attorney from Bijeljina. The request to undertake the investigation has been read of the military court in Bijeljina, IVTK, number 22/92, 2 -- January 1st 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to read the next paragraph, please, now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The accused has been informed that he does not have to defend himself, although in doing so, he can jeopardise his criminal and legal position, after which the accused stated that he wants to give his statement based on the request to undertake the investigation."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And underneath this text is your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did somebody force you to sign this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion and knowledge, yes, because I underwent so many beatings; therefore, I didn't dare to say a single word.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about your feelings; I asked you whether somebody forced you there on the spot to sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't talking about my feelings; I was talking about the beatings that I underwent and about my fear, and I signed everything because I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You again did not answer my question. Did somebody force you there, on that spot?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is now badgering the witness. The witness has made clear that he felt afraid whenever he signed documents. We still have not established whether this witness specifically remembers signing this page. He acknowledges the signature, that at some stage being required to sign some documents. He testified today, and this particular page that the counsel is now examining on, was one of the pages that, not through fault of Defence counsel but through clerical error was not disclosed to us. The witness saw it, read it for the first time after he had taken his oath when he was sitting here, and it has never established that he actually remembers, recalling signing this document, and now he's saying that when he signed things he felt afraid. So now -- this is now badgering the witness because he's being asked when he signed this particular document, again a fact in dispute whether or not someone forced him. So he cannot ask him if someone forced him to sign it when he doesn't specifically acknowledge signing this particular document or even recalls he may have signed any number of documents put to him during his time in detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has explained as to what had happened to him and his state of mind at the time. Counsel is asking whether if at all he did sign, at the time he was signing, was there somebody standing right there and telling him or ordering him to sign? I think that's the question of counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and our objection is still that counsel has not established that the witness recalls specifically signing this particular page. He acknowledges his signature, but he has not recalled signing this specific page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that is noted, Ms. Reidy. Yes. Perhaps the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you just to say whether somebody forced you or coerced you in any way when you were -- if you were signing this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the Prosecution on the 23rd of April, 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. What year?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: April 23rd, 1998, you gave a statement to the Prosecution of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you maybe read this statement now that you were in The Hague, before you testified here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you stand by this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I make it clear, because Mr. Lukic appears not to be putting it on the record. This is not a signed statement of the witness. It is a statement which was a short three-page statement which was taken indeed from the witness. It specifically says in bold at the end of it, "This statement was not read to the witness and, therefore, the witness has not had opportunity to verify or acknowledge the accuracy and truth of the statement." And the witness's signature appears nowhere on the statement. So if he wants to ask him whether he adopts specific things he says in it now, then the witness should at least be given the opportunity to read and address specific questions from counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is counsel -- okay. Let me wait for the interpretation to be completed. Mr. Lukic, does that statement you're holding have the contents spelled out by Ms. Reidy, saying that the statement was not read to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this statement does say that the -- that it was not reread to the witness, and therefore my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Your question was misleading to the witness, when you say: "Do you stand by this statement?" He could have said yes, not understanding the implication what he's answering to. So your question was misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I do not want to create any kind of a trap.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether you read the statement which you have not signed and whether you read it in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have enough time to read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you stand by everything that is stated in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. My statement -- I stand behind my statement of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you say at that time to the Prosecutor, and relevant to your interrogation in Bijeljina, the following question. I will read you - the following statement. I will read you what is stated in this document: "When the judge made his decision, he asked me to sign it. I refused to sign it, and the judge ordered police to take me to the correctional centre." Is that something you said in 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now you said, in front of the Chamber, that, out of fear, you signed the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please explain. Which is true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what you're looking for. I signed the statement out of fear, which you know, and you know even today that I have this fear. And it is true whether he gave me the statement on the very same day and whether I was taken to the correctional -- or when they first brought me to the correctional centre, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you said that you signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's important to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it's time to make a break now, Your Honours. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's two more minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We can have our break and resume at 1805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. You continue with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read out to you one more sentence from your statement to the OTP from year 1998, when you said the following, and it has to do with the same trial at the military court in Bijeljina: "After a while I was taken to the courthouse in Bijeljina. I was given a Serb defence counsel. I was not allowed to talk during the trial." During saying that to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so, yes. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were giving your statement to the OTP in 1998, you knew for a fact that a defence counsel had been assigned to you at the military court in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is something I heard from that policeman, but I was not shown around or told what was what and who was who.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But yesterday, in response to a question from the Prosecutor, you didn't say that you knew you had a defence counsel, a court-appointed lawyer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a long time ago. I can't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you were informed by the policeman there in the courtroom that a defence counsel had been assigned to you, but you were not introduced to him; is that correct? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like to introduce, only for identification again, one of those documents that I received from the file in the military court in Bijeljina, and again regrettably I only have the B/C/S version. I would like the witness to read out only one sentence. The document has been distributed to the OTP, and the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is entitled "Decision on the appointment of defence counsel."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number for identification only.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D39/3 ter ID, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I should like to ask you to read out the highlighted portion. There is a date at the top. You can read the title of the document and the highlighted section.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Decision on the appointment of defence counsel. The accused, Kemal Mehinovic, is assigned Ziko Krunic from Bijeljina as defence counsel. The accused, Kemal Mehinovic --"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the date at the top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 9th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that above the words "accused Kemal Mehinovic" there is wording that reads: "The following is notified to." Column.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And I am among those who are notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you have never seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I should now like to have shown to this witness document P56 ter ID, which we have already used today. You have analysed this document with the Prosecutor earlier today, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you to read the date at the top, and you said 27th March; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the military court in Bijeljina was located in the 27th March Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there is such a street named 27th March in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the 27th March is an important date in the history of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Below that date which you read out as the 27th of March, there are other numbers. Could you please read them, two lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only read the number, number 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And below that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's a 19 or a 9, January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was the date when you were before the investigating judge, as we ascertained.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please look again at this signature, which is poorly legible. Do you assert that this is not your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kemal -- this is not my signature. I sign differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about Mehinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Mehinovic part looks right, looks like mine, but the word, "Kemal" is almost printed, and I write differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you claim that you never signed this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now going to move on to a different topic. On page 86 of yesterday's transcript, you stated, and you confirmed to me, that in January 1993 you were taken to the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And a month after that you were taken to the correctional centre -- for a month after that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were taken there directly from the courthouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you spent there about a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you said that after that you were returned to Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did that happen, roughly? Was it the middle of February?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also said today that after returning to Batkovici, you saw Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you described that incident with Sabah Seric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His name was Sabah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you claim that it was after your arrival from the correctional centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also said you sighted him in July as well, in Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You never saw him after that, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are claiming before this Court that for the first time you saw Tadic was in December -- was in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After your appearance before the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the interpreter didn't get the year [sic], line 12, page 77, line 12. The first time you saw Tadic was in December -- maybe you can fill in the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I'm interested in knowing when you saw Tadic in Batkovici after you came back from the court and after the correctional centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You spent about a month in the correctional centre after you were brought back from the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you also said that you saw Tadic sometime in July of that year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So all of this is happening in year 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it was then that you saw Sabah Seric giving Tadic this 100 Deutschmark and promising him more money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was after you gave your statement to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're sure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show this witness document D25/3. I would like him to be shown the B/C/S version, D25/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document first, and then we can put it on the ELMO so that it is visible to others in the courtroom. Will you please read the person under number 24.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seric, son of Hasan, Sarhat [phoen], born 1950. That's not the same person. Sabah Seric is the son of Hasan, but he was born in Bosanski Samac in 1955.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lukic. Could you tell us what this document is? Because we're -- we have so many documents. We're a little bit in the dark here knowing what list this is until we see it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did indeed want to put it on the ELMO, but I wanted the witness to see it first. It is the list of people scheduled to be exchanged in Dragalic on the 15th of June, 1993, through the Exchange Commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you are claiming it's not the same man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know Saban Seric, who was born in 1950?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But this Sabah Seric also has the father by the name of Hasan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you claim that he left Batkovici after your return to Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...I don't think you are discussing --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The document is D25/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Is it the one dated --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Mumba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, is it the one dated the 24th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 24th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You claim that Saban Seric, son of Hasan, who gave money to Tadic, was exchanged later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't know any Saban Seric, son of Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How about Sabah Seric, son of Hasan, whom you claim gave money to Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said he was exchanged after you returned to Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was taken away from Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it's impossible that he was exchanged in December 1993 [sic]. Is it a frequent name, Sabah Seric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are perhaps three of them in Samac, but they don't have the same surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you in Batkovici in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you said a moment ago that Tadic was not visiting at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I was out working at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you saw him only when you were there on the spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned today his second coming to Batkovici. You said that he was standing together with the warden when a certain Dragan, little dragon, a soldier, assigned you into groups, Muslims on one side, Croats on another side, and people from Samac in the middle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This Dragan, little dragon, was he working in Batkovici as a guard or something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was one of the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did guards wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the warden wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in Batkovici the approval of the competent military authorities was required for someone to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another document that I would like to have marked for identification, from the same file of the criminal case, and I need to deal with only two or three sentences from this document with the witness. This is a communication from the collection centre in Batkovici, addressed to the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D40/3 ter ID, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, I don't suppose you saw this document before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please read out slowly the portions highlighted in yellow, starting from the top.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Collection centre, Batkovici, 18th February 1993. Military secret. Confidential. List of persons who are defendants in criminal proceedings. Hereby provided to the military court in Bijeljina. In response to your request, we are sending the list of persons who are defendants in criminal proceedings. Persons currently located at the collection centre: 1 -- number 9, Sead Mehinovic, son of Muradif, born 1956, Bosanski Samac." I don't know who this person is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, was your father's name Muradif?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And were you born in 1956 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So all of your personal details as indicated here are correct except for the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The name is not correct or the date. There is no date of birth, actually, just the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like you to look through the entire list. Is the date of birth indicated for anyone at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm only interested in myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you: Do you see the date of birth indicated for any other person? Answer me with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In February of 1993, you were in Batkovici; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think I was there. I was in the correctional centre in February. Maybe half of the month, early February or mid-February. I was returned on the 2nd -- I was returned in February, but I don't know on which date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in the second part of February you were returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was thinking of the second part of February, but I do not remember when exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you are not aware that the military authorities had to give their approval?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether you know the name of the warden of the correctional centre that you -- into whose office you went when Tadic was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was there, three persons occupied that position. I think at that point -- I'm not quite sure. I think it was Djoko Pajic, Major Djoko Pajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were detained, both the TO and later in Batkovici, did you manage to have any kind of a communication going with your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were at the TO building, did you have any communication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But after you were released from prison, she told you that she went -- she was exchanged in March of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We communicated in Batkovici through the International Red Cross. I was informed about my wife's exchange after they couldn't find her in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you told the Prosecutor - that's why I'm interested in this. When did she tell you this. She said she didn't want to be exchanged. She told you this when you were released, after you were released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then she told you that she and the children were released in the summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did she tell you at that time that earlier she had registered to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. She didn't tell me that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did she not mention this to you at all, that she registered with the International Red Cross for voluntary exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I think the witness said that the wife said nothing of that kind to him. Counsel has said it again. If he has evidence that she registered with the International Red Cross for the exchange, then let him put that. He certainly has disclosed no evidence to the Prosecution of that effect and I let it go once when he asked him, but he asked him again and the witness simply said no, the wife never said to him that she registered. So again, I object to him constantly asking the question when he's again putting evidence on the record which is not before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, he can cross-examine along the lines that he did, because one assumes that when the Defence case opens, he will support that challenge, the Defence will support that challenge to the Prosecution witness. Mr. Lukic, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's exactly the point, because I intend in my proceedings to show what the procedure was to register for exchange with the IRC. I have two further questions. I would like the witness to be shown the document introduced by the Prosecutor. I need to find the number. It's a list of exchanges when his wife and children were exchanged. If the Prosecutor could help me with this, I'd be very grateful. I just need the number of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm following the same transcript as Defence counsel. I believe it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it is. I have it. It's P58 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I only have one question, Mr. Mehinovic. Could you please read out what is said under 102.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Srna Hanka. I can read here. It says she returned, and it says 1935. It might be her date of birth -- her year of birth, but I'm not quite sure what's said in the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Frankly, I can't read it either. Did you know this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Srna Hanka. I'm not sure. I think this was the mother of Mirsad Srna, who was with me. He was detained with me [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar from what your wife told you, or personally, that certain people refused to be exchanged and they returned home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think we discussed this. I was not in any mood to have this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I asked you before whether you remember anything that has to do with this exchange, when Tadic came to TO - this means we're going back to the first period - do you remember the name of any of the people that were exchanged at that time when Tadic came, somebody who was with you at the TO? If you could think about it a little bit, because it would assist us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think it might have been Muhamed Bicic and Zlatko Radic. There were more Croats. I'm not quite sure what happened that day, but I think those two people were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The next counsel to cross-examine? Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Zaric's Defence I will conduct the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mehinovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic. I am Defence counsel of Mr. Simo Zaric. I'm going to lead this cross-examination. Before I begin with my questions, I would like to express my client's regret because of what you suffered in Bosnia. He asked me to express this to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before I begin with my questions, I would like you to have in mind what my colleague Mr. Lukic already reminded you of. If we could be very short in the answers, if you could answer with "yes" or "no" or "I do not know." If a certain question is not clear, could you please let me know that you do not understand the question so that I could make it clearer. In that way, we could shorten this procedure and save some time to the Court. Mr. Mehinovic, during the Prosecutor's examination, you were asked and you were also looking at a document - you were asked to identify certain persons of Muslim ethnicity that were members of the 4th Detachment. You did that quite quickly and well, and I would think that you are a good witness, with whom we could clear up some issues with the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, do you know when the 4th Detachment was founded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, you have never seen a list of the members of the 4th Detachment written on a paper, a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, because this question was -- started with a negation, which means that your "yes" means that you did not see the list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I did not see any lists of the 4th Detachment, but it doesn't mean that the people that I listed today are the exclusive members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I'm suggesting at all. You also did not see a list of the command of the 4th Detachment, in other words, those people that were commanding that detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Also you have never seen the 4th Detachment in a line, in other words, you never saw the members of the 4th Detachment at the same place, at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was a member of the Yugoslav national army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, have you ever heard of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While you were giving your statement and while you were being interrogated by the Prosecutor, you mentioned Mr. Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this Nikolic that you mentioned was the commander of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You also said before this Chamber that there were certain issues about -- that you talked to your friend Danilo about joining the 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to identify this person, is this Vitomir Danilo? Is that his full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know his last name, but he always used to say my Gavro, Gavro was his father. If this person's father is also named Gavro, that would be the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's clear this up again. Is this person Danilo, is that the same person that was wounded by Adis Izetbegovic before all these events and also Srna Safet? Is this the same person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's the same person, but I do not know who he was wounded by.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But in any case, you know he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With some other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You said during the Prosecutor's examination that even before the outbreak of hostilities in Samac, members of the 4th Detachment were wearing civilian clothes and that they carried weapons underneath their clothes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you never saw them in uniforms around Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There were no uniforms at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this carrying of weapons underneath clothes, how could you be sure that it was weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because some of them -- with some of them you could see parts of the weapons while they were moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you be a little bit more precise with regard to this? Could you tell me exactly the name or the last name of that person or those persons which sometimes would reveal as having weapons underneath their clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this Danilo, and then also there was Atic Muhamed, with the nickname Hamko, a very good friend of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we have dealt enough with the 4th Detachment. Now I would like to move on to another topic. [In English] Your Honours, at this moment I believe that I'm going to ask for a closed session, because I will mention certain name of a witness that was protected, and I cannot assert to this witness, Witness A, B, C, D, or something, because I do need to use his name. It will take maybe two minutes, not more, but I believe it is a good moment, because after that I won't need the closed session any further until the end of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go into I think private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, let's move on to this day now, the 17th of April of 1992. You have already given your statement that has to do with these events. The statement was very detailed. I would now be interested only in certain details that I think we could clear up a bit further. You said that early in the morning, around 6.00, you started going towards your bakery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that you came to the bakery and that you met your brother, who told you to go home. I am interested to know about this. It's early in the morning, at 6.00, you're going towards the bakery. Did you see any fighting in the city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers at that point, from 6.00 onward, until you came back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you maybe see any military vehicles, transporters, any kind of military equipment moving about the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of my house towards the bakery, no, I did not see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
