utterances.text: So after this, you come back home, and you said that around 8.00, 8.30 you met a group of people, including brothers Bicic, Hasan and Muhamed, Ibrahim Salkic, and some other young men, all together maybe around 20 people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, in order to go faster, I would like to give you some names, and you will tell me whether these names belong to the people that were there along with brothers, Salkic and others, if you remember. I will be reading you names, one after another, and you will be saying "yes" if they were members of that group; if they were not, you would say "no," and that's how we will proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is there also an option of me saying, "I don't know"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. First one: Dzakic Damir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Ferhat Sahacic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Muharem Drljacic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mirsad Srna.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Salko Srna.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Muharem Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Suad Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fadil Sabanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Esad Dagovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Safet Dagovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Osman Mesic, nicknamed Semso.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Atic Ratif, called Raif.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you already said that Atic Kemal, called Kilo, was already there, so that's already been covered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me please say something. If that is -- if this is true, it is known. I did mention in my statement Ibela's group was going from the pensioners' retirement home when we were going from the school towards the department store. Then certain other people joined us, like Dedo, Atic, and also a young man called Safet Srna. There's a difference here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this explanation. So this group, without these people that you mentioned just now -- I just wanted to ask you, because you were mentioning the school: There is a primary school and a secondary school in Samac. Did you go up to the primary or the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The street is right next to the school yard, at the very end of Vuk Karadzic Street. That's the primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So when you were coming back from the school, from the direction of the school, you were joined by a certain other number of citizens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think we're speaking the same language. Please explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have said enough. I saw 20 young men who were going from the direction of the retirement home to the school, and I joined them when I left my home, but I never said that other people joined.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I said when they were coming back from there. You just told me about Atic and Dedo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This was in the city centre. This has nothing to do with the school or up to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not want to suggest anything about the answer, and I assume that now we have reached an understanding about what happened. So now we're talking about this first group that is going towards Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the school. You had already mentioned that they were armed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: They told you that they were going to Donja Mahala to defend their people from the massacre. I think that's the expression you used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you went with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While you were going towards the school, did you maybe see any military in that part of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From your answers, I would say that my next question is maybe superfluous, but I will ask it anyway. Was anybody shooting at you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Neither was the group that you were in shooting at anybody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While you were going there, and during your return, did you maybe see Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe my question was a little bit early. I should have asked you first: Do you know Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you joined the group that told you that they were going to Donja Mahala to defend their people -- their nation, their people, against murder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But you were not armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehinovic, according to your statement and what you heard from them, you were going to a location at which a massacre was taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you were not taking any weapons with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you think that you would protect the people with your bare hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't think anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will ask only one more question, because we are at the end of today's session. You said that Ibrahim Salkic, Ibela, was in front of this Carrington building, which belonged to a certain person called Biber, and that he had a walkie-talkie and that he went into the house and that he told you later that he talked to Lieutenant Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was this discussion, this talk that Salkic had with Nikolic, influential in any way so that the tension in this group was a little bit alleviated and people went home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn our proceedings until tomorrow at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I elicit from Defence counsel if they have any idea how long they think the cross might take, just so I can advise Victim/Witness but also as to when the next witness will be available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lazarevic, How much more do you think it will take?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hope that it won't take more than one hour, maybe one hour and a half, but I don't believe that it will take more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, half an hour, 40 minutes, maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think less than half an hour, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Ms. Reidy, I think you can work that one out. The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of May, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
